interpretations: For each sex, average its valid CPK/GPT test ratios; retain sex averages above the mean of all sex averages, then above the mean of the retained sex averages. Report the mean of the final sex averages and its absolute differences from both thresholds.
Apply the same two sex-level filters, then pool all valid tests from the remaining sexes. Report the pooled mean ratio and its absolute differences from both thresholds.

Use the mean of individual test ratios from the first-stage sexes as the second threshold; retain sexes whose average exceeds it. Report the mean of their sex averages and its absolute differences from both thresholds.

After the first sex-level filter, retain only individual tests whose ratio exceeds their own sex’s average. Report the mean ratio of those tests and its absolute differences from the first-stage mean and their respective sex averages.
Read “above their own mean” literally as requiring each retained sex’s average to exceed that same sex’s average; no sex qualifies, so the single result row contains missing aggregates.

For each sex, calculate the ratio of its mean CPK to its mean GPT using tests with a valid ratio; then apply the two sex-level filters and report the final mean and its distances above both thresholds.

After the first sex-level filter, keep tests whose ratios exceed their own sex’s mean, recalculate an average for each remaining sex, then report the mean of those sex averages and its distances above both thresholds.
queries:
WITH sex_averages AS (
    SELECT p.SEX, AVG(1.0 * l.CPK / l.GPT) AS avg_ratio
    FROM Patient AS p
    JOIN Laboratory AS l ON l.ID = p.ID
    WHERE p.SEX IS NOT NULL
      AND l.CPK IS NOT NULL
      AND l.GPT IS NOT NULL
      AND l.GPT <> 0
    GROUP BY p.SEX
),
first_threshold AS (
    SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS threshold FROM sex_averages
),
retained AS (
    SELECT avg_ratio
    FROM sex_averages
    WHERE avg_ratio > (SELECT threshold FROM first_threshold)
),
second_threshold AS (
    SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS threshold FROM retained
),
final_average AS (
    SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS mean_ratio
    FROM retained
    WHERE avg_ratio > (SELECT threshold FROM second_threshold)
)
SELECT f.mean_ratio,
       ABS(f.mean_ratio - t1.threshold) AS difference_from_first_threshold,
       ABS(f.mean_ratio - t2.threshold) AS difference_from_second_threshold
FROM final_average AS f
CROSS JOIN first_threshold AS t1
CROSS JOIN second_threshold AS t2

SELECT AVG(sex_mean)
FROM (
    SELECT AVG(ID) AS sex_mean
    FROM Patient
    GROUP BY SEX
    HAVING AVG(ID) > AVG(ID)
)
